about.title: Ventura Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Public collision records show nine traffic deaths in Ventura in 2025. Each of those numbers was a parent, a partner, a son or daughter — someone whose absence is now felt at a kitchen table somewhere off Telegraph Road or Victoria Avenue. If you are reading this because you lost someone that way, or because a fall, a defective product, or a medical error took them, you are not looking for statistics. California gives certain family members the right to bring a wrongful death claim. Spouses, domestic partners, and children stand first in line; other dependents and heirs may qualify when there is no surviving spouse or child. The claim is civil, separate from anything a prosecutor in Ventura County decides to do, and it generally must be filed within two years of the date of death — sooner if a city, county, or state agency is involved. Our team handles wrongful death claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. Our team can walk you through where your family fits before anyone spends time on paperwork.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is considerably shorter when a public agency is involved. Getting our team involved sooner keeps those dates from slipping.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We handle wrongful death cases on contingency. Grieving families should not have to weigh legal bills against pursuing accountability.

items.question: What can a Ventura family actually recover in a wrongful death case?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. The specifics depend on your relationship to the person and the circumstances of the death. Our team can explain how these categories apply to your family without making promises about amounts.

items.question: The driver who hit my husband on Telegraph Road is facing charges. Do I have to wait for that case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, entirely separate from anything the Ventura County District Attorney pursues. You can move forward regardless of whether criminal charges are filed, dropped, or result in a conviction. Waiting can actually work against you because the two-year civil deadline keeps running.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact us?
items.answer: Nothing. Our team handles wrongful death cases on contingency. That means no fee unless there is a recovery, and the first conversation carries no obligation.
